open Finset EuclideanGeometry Filter

namespace Erdos98

/-- $h(n)$ is the minimum number of distinct distances determined by any
$n$-point set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ in general position (no three collinear, no four
cocyclic). -/
noncomputable def h (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ points : Finset ℝ², points.card = n ∧
    InGeneralPosition points ∧ k = distinctDistances points}

/--
Let $h(n)$ be such that any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line
and no four on a circle, determine at least $h(n)$ distinct distances. Does
$h(n)/n\to \infty$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_98 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((h n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős could not even prove $h(n)\geq n$. Pach has shown $h(n) < n^{\log_2 3}$.
Erdős, Füredi, and Pach [EFPR93] have improved this to
$h(n) < n\exp(c\sqrt{\log n})$ for some constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_98.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (h n : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) * Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt (Real.log (n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos98

reformulations.difference: Lean takes the infimum of achieved distance counts, whereas Er83c defines h(n) as the largest integer guaranteed as a lower bound for every admissible configuration.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Admissible configurations exist for every n: choose n distinct points (t,t²) with t>0. A line contains at most two of these points. Four on a circle would give four positive roots of a monic quartic with zero cubic coefficient, contradicting their positive sum. Thus the set of achieved natural-number counts is nonempty, and its infimum is an attained minimum. Consequently k ≤ h(n) exactly when every admissible n-point set determines at least k distances. This characterization was proved in scratch Lean conditional on existence; the geometric existence argument was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: Lean bounds h(n) for sufficiently large n using exp(c√log n), while EFPR93 Theorem 3.1 states existence of configurations for each positive n with a base-2 exponential bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since h(n) is attained, a bound on h(n) is equivalent to existence of an admissible configuration satisfying that bound. The identity 2^(c√log n) = exp((c log 2)√log n) absorbs the exponential base into the unspecified constant. Increasing the constant handles positivity and any strict-versus-nonstrict distinction for n≥2. An eventual bound extends to all positive n by further increasing the constant to cover the finitely many exceptions n≥2, since √log n>0; n=1 already satisfies the bound because h(1)=0. Conversely an all-positive-n bound implies the eventual bound.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations, answer scope, shared geometric definitions, natural-number infimum semantics, and filter domains. Scratch files /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/metric-tests.lean compile successfully without using the problem theorems as proof inputs. Tests establish h(0)=h(1)=0, h(2)=1, exclusion of zero self-distances, the Euclidean 3–4–5 distance, and the three-/four-element-subset interpretation of general position. Division and logarithm defaults at n=0 do not affect either asymptotic statement. Full texts of Er90, Er94b and Er97e could not be retrieved; all declarations were nevertheless directly checked against other cited primary sources. No repository files were modified.
